Where we are right now

Where we are (US): Day 1 sold 1,312 units against 1,198 planned (+10%) at a 9.17% TACoS. Deal products spent $4,433 on ads against a $1,962 plan (2.3×). Profit after the 7.5% reserve is $5.6K on the board; on Sellerboard's costs, adjusted to the same basis, it is about $7.5K. Either way the US beat its plan, carried by the discount and organic sales, not by PPC: ad ACoS was 31–41% on the three deal products against break-evens of 10.6–17.8%. Day 2 at 06:48 PT: 161 units vs 168 planned, estimated profit $368 vs $431 planned; pace B4 1.18, B6 1.01, S4 0.64.

Your Sellerboard screenshot, reconciled

The screenshot (Oct 6: sales $89,447, 1,721 units, ads $7,821, net profit $12,900, TACoS 8.74%) is the whole account, US + Canada in USD. 01

Bamboo 4pc (B4) · PED 20% · US

DecisionReduce + Reallocate
DirectionSales and profit ahead of plan; spend going the wrong way

Day 1 beat the plan on units (+29%), revenue (+33%) and profit (+95%), but ad spend ran at 2.0× plan and TACoS hit 8.97% against a 6% cap. The overspend has one main cause: three autos took 54% of campaign spend ($1,141) because the event-night T9 run put rest-of-search premiums of +377% to +692% on them, and the event layer only zeroed the top-of-search side. The money the plan meant for the Cooling and Twin pushes and the main "bamboo sheets" exacts went to autos and clearance instead. Day 2 so far (to 06:00 PT) is running at 3.8% TACoS after the Day-1 fixes, so the job now is to keep it there and stop the Oct 8 reverts from re-arming the premiums.

1Plan vs target vs Day-1 results

Plan: PED at 20% ($59.99 King), 290 units, $17.4K revenue, $1,042 of ads (6% TACoS cap), $1,226 profit after reserve; objective "Push King, Cooling; bamboo sheets = profit". Result: 373 units, $23.1K, $2,071 of ads, $2,394 profit. Direction: right on sales and profit, wrong on spend and on the ranking objective. The profit beat came from the discount and organic sales (about 77% of units), not from PPC efficiency: ad ACoS was 32% against a 17.8% break-even.

2Hour by hour

The day had one clear break at 10:39–11:20 PT. Before it, SP spend ran $1,114 at a $3.39 CPC with only 16% at top of search and cumulative TACoS peaked at 14% at 04:00 PT. After M8 removed the auto rest-of-search premiums (10:39) and M13/M14 removed the PP/ROS premiums (11:20), CPC fell to $1.1–2.0 and TOS share rose to 20–58% while units held at about 21 an hour. Capped campaigns climbed from 1 at midnight to 25 by 23:00, so the afternoon ran on whatever still had budget. The evening peak (18:00–19:00, 62 units on $290) was efficient. No tool reports campaign-level hourly spend; campaign timing is rebuilt from run-out times and change timestamps, marked on the chart.

Reading. The product-level hourly data shows one break: before 11:00 PT the SP CPC ran $2.9-$4.2 with TOS share 7-25%; from 11:00 PT (first full hour after M8 removed the auto ROS premiums at 10:39 and M13/M14 removed PP/ROS premiums at 11:20) CPC fell to $1.1-$2.0 and TOS share rose to 20-58%, while units held (hours 11-19 averaged 21/hr vs 18/hr in 3-10). Cumulative TACoS peaked at 14.0% at 04:00 PT and fell steadily to 8.97%. Capped campaigns climbed from 1 (00:00) to 14 (10:00) and 25 (23:00) - the pushes and autos ran out early, so the afternoon ran on whatever still had budget. No campaign-level hourly tool exists; per-campaign timing is reconstructed from run-out times and decision timestamps only.

Spikes and drops, with the likely reason: - 03:00–10:59 PT, high-CPC block. SP spend was $1,114 at a CPC of $3.39 and TOS share of 16%. The T9 auto ROS premiums were live, and the pushes ran out of budget between 03:15 and 10:44. - 11:00 PT, step down. CPC fell to $1.95 and TOS share rose to 34–48%. This follows M8, which zeroed the auto ROS premiums at 10:39, and M13/M14, which removed the PP and ROS premiums at 11:20. - 13:00–14:00 PT, spend trough ($36–39 per hour). This follows the M18 push taper at 12:24 and the cumulative run-outs (17–18 campaigns capped). Units held at 16–22 per hour. - 15:00 PT dip in conversion. Spend was $72 for 10 units. This was the first hour after the M26 budget raises, with clicks moving onto PAT and defence. - 18:00–19:00 PT evening peak. 62 units on $290 of spend at about $1.6 CPC. - 20:00 PT drop to $30 per hour. The aged-deal LTSF auto ($500) ran out at 20:06. - Oct 7, 00:00–05:00 PT. TACoS was 3.8% and CPC $1.41, with profit after reserve at $280.67 against a plan of $88.59. The Day-1 fixes are holding. TOS share reached 52% at 05:00 PT, the first full hour after M48 re-enabled the queen "bamboo cooling sheets" exact at TOS +618%; check this at 10:00 PT.

3Ranking campaigns

The ranking push is not working. 34 ranking campaigns spent $371 at 32% ACoS (break-even 17.8%); 25 of them took no order. Checked against the pre-event daily range, only "bamboo sheets twin" (50 → 18) improved beyond normal noise, and only on DataRova (Data Dive shows no gain; 12 of its 14 clicks came through the LTSF auto, so the exact can't take the credit). "cooling bamboo sheets" (12 → 43) and "bamboo cooling sheets king size" (25 → 32) are worse than any pre-event day on DataRova, but Data Dive says "cooling bamboo sheets" improved to 10, so it is inconclusive. The main Cooling exact (SV 8,166) was paused all of Day 1 and its own rank held 28–30, so the pause did not cause a Cooling loss. Root causes: the event layer cut push budgets to $5 overnight (dark from 03:15 to 06:05 PT), and push bids were priced on the full-price margin, so TOS clicks cost $6.5–10 against a deal-price maximum of about $1.80–1.95.

Detailed analysis · Campaign review
Exact / ranking (34 spending campaigns, $383.71)

Exact is the ranking layer. Every push paid a TOS ranking premium of $4.5–$10 per click against a break-even ceiling near $1.2 at the prior CVR. That is legitimate only while the rank moves (SOP 23). Twin moved (bamboo sheets twin 50 → 18). Cooling did not: four cooling keywords were at or worse than their worst pre-event day on Oct 7. The out-of-focus exact campaigns, including the main "bamboo sheets" VHSV exact, were tapered to near zero. Branded exact ran inside break-even.

Detailed analysis · Ranking review

B4 – Bamboo 4pc (59) · objective "Push King, Cooling (bamboo sheets = profit)" · BE 17.8%

Verdict: the ranking push is not working. We are spending without a demonstrated rank improvement. - Spend: 34 ranking campaigns spent $371.47, which is 19.7% of the $1,884.91 attributed product spend. - Efficiency: ACoS was 32.2% against a 17.8% break-even, so $166.30 of the spend was above break-even. 88.5% of it was at TOS. 25 of the 34 campaigns took 0 orders ($173.97). - Rank result: only "bamboo sheets twin" moved beyond its noise band, and only on DR. Two push terms ended Oct 7 worse than any pre-event day on DR.

Cooling rank-loss diagnosis. The coordinator's point stands: the main Cooling exact was dark all of Day 1 and five Cooling exacts were funded only on Oct 7. - The only Cooling term that "fell" on DR ("cooling bamboo sheets", to 43) improved on DD, to 10 with sponsored #3. - The main term itself held at 28–30 with no ads. - So a Cooling rank loss is not established. What is established is that Cooling money was spread across about 14 low-volume exacts while the SV-8,166 term was dark.

Structure issues (SOP 23 / 28 / 32)
  1. The event cap made the push go dark. The T11 1.25× cap set a $5 floor on push exacts at 20:49–20:53 PT Oct 5, minutes after T9 raised the same budgets. B4 push exacts were dark from their first run-out (03:15–06:03 PT) until 06:05 PT. This breaks SOP-23 G3 (truncated campaigns) and SOP-32 P3 (caps written as decisions, not silent stops).
  2. Ceilings were priced on the full-price margin. The decision record prices push ceilings on the non-deal margin: #5624 uses "break-even 35.5%", and #5506 targets $5.81 against a "$3.65 break-even ceiling". At the deal price, break-even is 17.8%, which means a maximum profitable CPC of about $1.80–1.95. SOP-32 P4 step 3 names this error. No M2 worksheet or loss ceiling exists for any push (SOP-23 F1).
  3. Pushes were logged under a quarantine verdict. T9 "QUARANTINE: DATA REFRESH" decisions still raised TOS to +463%, +604% and +900% (Twin Sheets Bamboo). Under SOP-23 G1, a quarantined row produces a flag, never a push.
  4. Ranking budget sits on low-volume terms. There are about 30 ranking exacts, many LSV, VLSV or NOSV (SOP-23 P1 step 4 sets a 500-SV floor), while the SV-8,166 Cooling exact was paused.
  5. Duplicates and in-window structure changes: - Two campaigns target "bamboo cooling sheets king size". - A "deep pocket" variant was created Oct 5 20:42 PT, at arming (SOP-32 freeze list / SOP-23 F13). - An MSV "King Size Sheets Set Bamboo Cooling" duplicate was correctly paused. - Eight twin exacts each have a $5–25 budget.
  6. Auto and LTSF campaigns carry push terms. The LTSF auto takes "bamboo sheets twin" (12 of 14 clicks) and "bamboo sheets" (87 of 96). Under SOP-23 F10 the rank cannot be credited to the exacts. Walls (SOP-29) should go in after the event, not in-window.
  7. Sibling conflict. B4 and B6 both bid "bamboo sheets" and King terms (B4 "Bamboo Sheets King Size HSV" exact $3.27, alongside B6's). SOP-23 G11 names the open Bamboo root ownership.
  8. Modifiers above the 300% ceiling: Twin Sheets Bamboo +900%, main Cooling exact +618% (pending +718%). Pending Oct 8 legs would re-raise others (modifier audit, section e).

4Auto / Broad / Phrase (and Exact, PAT)

Auto (57% of spend, ACoS 39%): the two discovery autos converted well (12–20% CVR) but paid 5.9–6.5× their normal CPC because of the ROS premiums; the aged-deal LTSF auto ($501, $23.87 per order) had a $500 budget and no event cap. Broad (14%, ACoS 24%): the branded defensive broad was the best large campaign (20% CVR) but 92% of its spend landed on product pages at $3.20 because of a PP +100% modifier, while TOS on the same terms cost $1.39 and converted at 22%. Phrase barely ran ($15.64, LTSF twin phrase, 0 orders). Exact (18%) is the ranking set above. PAT (10%, ACoS 19%): own-ASIN defence converted at 10.5% ACoS; the new conquest PAT took $48 for no orders.

Detailed analysis · Campaign review

2. What drove the results

  • The autos took the event. Spend by match type was Auto 57% ($1,201, ACoS 39%), Exact 18% ($384, 31%), Broad 14% ($303, 24%) and PAT 10% ($203, 19%). In the baseline the mix per day was Exact 61%, Broad 25%, PAT 6%, Auto 6%.
  • Mechanism. At 20:41–20:42 PT on Oct 5, the T9 "PLACEMENT PROFIT" run wrote rest-of-search (ROS) premiums onto the discovery autos: +692% on the Full-Grey auto (base $0.60), +463% on the King-White auto (base $0.87) and +377% on the B4 LTSF auto. The T11 event layer zeroed only the top-of-search (TOS) legs, at 21:17 PT. The ROS premiums stayed live through the night and the morning peak until M8 set them to 0 at 10:39 PT Oct 6. Over that time the autos paid $4.19–$4.80 per ROS click on $0.60–$0.87 bids. The Full-Grey auto spent $337 against a $10/day baseline. The King-White auto spent $303 against $1.30/day. SOP 28 P2 (the ceiling worksheet must clear before any modifier change) would have blocked both moves. SOP 32 P4.1 also applies: the default modifier posture in an event window is "no change".
  • The aged-deal LTSF auto had no cap. It ran on a $500 budget, outside the campaign registry (no objective), so neither T11 nor the hourly desk governed it. It spent $501 for 21 orders: ACoS 36.7%, $23.87 per order. SOP 32 P3 calls an affected campaign with no cap failure mode F1. M55 paused its three worst aged colours only at 04:26 PT on Oct 7.
  • What worked. Every campaign below ran under break-even:
  • Branded and own-ASIN defence: Decolure_SP_Exact_PAT_Defensive at 10.5% ACoS; PAT on the hero ASIN B08KQHRDDG at 15.3%; branded exact at 15.1%.
  • Queen exact "bamboo sheets queen" at 9.9% (5 orders on 11 clicks).
  • Twin White push "bamboo sheets twin" at 8.8% (3 orders on 3 clicks). Its rank went 50 → 42 → 18.
  • The ranking pushes moved in opposite directions.
  • Twin rose on the Oct 7 crawl: "bamboo sheets twin" 42→18, "twin sheets bamboo" 25→17, "bamboo sheets twin size" 25→19, "twin bamboo sheets" 28→21.
  • Cooling fell: "cooling bamboo sheets" 9 (Oct 4) → 12 → 18 → 43; "bamboo cooling sheets king size" 13→32. Both of those are worse than any pre-event day (rank_noise.json). "bamboo sheets cooling" 19→40, "cooling sheets bamboo" 12→40 and "cooling king bed sheets" 13→60 also fell, but "bamboo sheets cooling" stays inside its 12–40 pre-event range, so treat these three as noise until confirmed. Of the twin moves, only "bamboo sheets twin" is better than any pre-event day.
  • The cooling pushes paid $6.5–$9.6 per TOS click. Five of them ran out of budget between 03:15 and 10:44 PT. In-window ranks are provisional (SOP 32 S-E5), but the cooling direction is negative.
  • The main syntax exact campaigns were tapered, not consolidated on (Erik #1). The event-night run focused on Bamboo|Cooling and Bamboo|Twin. Everything else was marked "out of focus": TOS was zeroed, bids were cut ×0.682 and budgets were cut.

By campaign-name SKU, Oct 6 spend was: King White $822 (40 orders, ACoS 29%), multi-SKU autos and LTSF $601, Full-Grey auto $337, Queen White $180, Twin "Burgundy-named" campaigns (now Navy or White) $57.

C. Sections by campaign type (CPC/CVR behaviour, bid appropriateness, role)

Rule: BE max CPC = AOV $64.72 x 17.8% x CVR (Oct 6 CVR if >=15 clicks, else 13-day baseline if >=15 clicks, else product 10.2%). Ranking campaigns may run above it only under a funded push (SOP 23) - flagged, not called overbid.. Break-even cost per order is $11.52. Search-term and negation detail is in d1/negation.*, prepared by another agent.

Auto (6 spending campaigns, $1201.20)

Autos were the biggest problem of the event. The two discovery autos converted well (12–20% CVR), but they paid 5.9–6.5× their baseline CPC because the T9 ROS premium multiplied tiny bases. Their role is discovery, and they behaved like the main sales engine without the economics of one. The aged-deal LTSF auto is LTSF, so judge it on cost per aged unit ($23.87 per order), not on ACoS. Bid order breaks SOP 15 (close > substitutes > loose > complements): in the Full-Grey auto all three groups sit at $0.60, and loose-match took 60% of its spend at 65.7% ACoS.

5Negation review

Little true Day-1 waste sits in Auto/Broad/Phrase search terms; the big zero-order spend is in exact and PAT campaigns at $7–10 TOS clicks, which is a bid/placement problem, not a negation case. Do not negate "bamboo sheets" in the aged-deal LTSF auto now, even though it took 88% of that term's spend: it converted there (4 orders on Day 1, 165 in 30 days) and the hero exact is held at $0.83 for the event, so a wall would cut live orders. Cut the auto's bid and budget instead and re-read after Oct 13. Workbook phrases flagged but never deployed kept spending (e.g. "split" terms: 18 clicks, $81, 0 orders) — those go in now. 9 converting or push terms are walled out of their source campaigns and lost all paid coverage once their exact ran out of budget; four B4 walls were breached on Day 1 and need a landing check.

6Placement

Top of search fell from 63% to 21% of spend while converting at 21% against 8.6% (ROS) and 10.1% (PP). TOS cost $15.9 per order vs $27.3 at ROS. The plan wanted TOS on ranking terms; the T9 premiums sent the money to ROS. Where TOS should get more: the defensive broad (cut PP +100% → 0 and lift the base bid to $1.90 so the same terms buy TOS at about $1.90), the "bamboo sheets queen size" broad and "100 Bamboo" broad (TOS +50%, earned on baseline), the aged-deal LTSF auto (TOS +50%, TOS CVR 17% vs 4.6%). Where ROS/PP must stay at 0: both discovery autos, the queen-size broad and the PAT on King White (PP +57% bought 0 orders).

On Day 1, TOS converted at 2.4× ROS and cost $15.9 per order, against $27.3 per order at ROS. TOS was still above the $11.52 break-even cost per order, but it was the best placement. Spend went the other way: TOS share collapsed from 63% to 21%. The ROS premium is the reason.

Efficient campaigns with low TOS share. These pass three tests: TOS under 30% of the campaign's spend, TOS CVR at least 1.3× the rest, and TOS CPC at or under break-even CPC. Each premium needs a booked removal (SOP 28 §1.3 TOS-EARNS; SOP 32 P4.2):

7Stock and inventory

Inventory is not limiting the push. 7,038 FBA + 8,604 inbound; cover 19 days at Day-1 pace, 33 at Day-2 pace, 102 at normal pace. The push SKU King White has 1,784 units (225 days at normal pace). Queen White is the constraint: 51 units, about 12 days left after the event, and its Oct 20 shipment is flagged overdue — keep the 55 Queen campaigns on Queen Light Blue (217 units, ~32 days even with Queen White's demand) and swap back only when Queen White shows ≥ 250 units. Twin White (5.3 days at deal pace) stays on Navy. Full White is out of stock: move its 8 campaigns to Full Light Blue (100). "purple bamboo sheets" advertises Queen Purple (4 units) — move to Full Purple (76).

Verdict. Plan: PED both days; push King (board objective 'Push King'); Day-1 plan 290 units → Target: hero variations White/Black per size with >= window+14 d cover (SOP-32 G6) → Day 1: 373 units (129% of plan); King White 42, Queen White 27 (deal 28/29 sold), King Navy 24 → Gap: Queen White hit its deal cap and fell to 51 FBA; ETA of its 678-unit NJ shipment is Oct 20 (tracker flags it overdue) → Root cause: Queen White deal allocation (29) sold on Day 1 while 732 units are still inbound → Direction correct? Yes - M36 rotation (Oct 6 ~18:12) moved 55 Queen campaigns to Queen Light Blue and 3 ASIN-target campaigns to King White; King White (1,784 FBA, 225 d normal) is the right stock sink → Action: Keep the rotation; do not swap back early. Re-point the 8 Full ranking campaigns off out-of-stock Full White and the purple keyword off Queen Purple (4 units) (see swaps). No new push on King Navy (24 units Day 1 without ads, 126 FBA). → Expected: Queen demand served from Light Blue (217 FBA covers ~32 d at Light Blue + Queen White normal pace 6.7/d) until Queen White restocks; no paid clicks into a stockout.

8Allocation vs actual

The plan put the money on the Bamboo|Cooling and Bamboo|Twin exact pushes and brand defence, with discovery and profit campaigns stripped of premiums. The reverse happened: exact ranking fell from 61% of normal spend to 18%, autos rose from 1% to 30% (55× their normal day) and LTSF autos took another 28%. Brand defence ran 3.5× normal at 17.1% ACoS, the only group inside break-even. Decision: cap the autos and the LTSF auto, put the freed budget only where it earns (defence, Queen exact, Twin White) and keep pushes priced to the deal margin.

Detailed analysis · Campaign review

6. Budget and bid efficiency

  • Run-outs (board list).
  • Push campaigns ran out early: Bamboo Sheets Cooling 03:15, Cooling Bamboo Sheets 05:07, bamboo cool sheets 05:51, Twin Bamboo Bed Sheets 06:03, Cooling Sheets Bamboo 10:21, Bamboo Cooling Sheets King Size 10:44, Bamboo Sheets Twin 14:10.
  • The two autos ran out at 04:10 ($400) and 07:13 ($350). The defensive broad ran out at 08:15 ($200). The LTSF aged-deal auto ran out at 20:06 ($500).
  • Several board budgets disagree with the decision record. The flags are in the JSON.
  • The event cap mechanism hurt the pushes. T11 set push budgets to 1.25× normal spend with a $5 floor, then the desk had to restore them during the day:
  • 06:05 PT: mock-read restore to the audit values.
  • 14:33 PT: M26 raises.
  • Oct 7 03:51 PT: M46–M48 raises.
  • Several budgets also changed outside the record. The twin pushes went from 5 to 20/15/10.
  • Effective TOS bids on the pushes ran above the plan's declared price. "cooling bamboo sheets" was bid at $7.76 against a plan of $5.81 and a break-even CPC of about $2.10. M18 capped several at the 300% ceiling. "Cooling Sheets Bamboo" is still at +380%.
  • Sample sizes are too small for bid reads. Every push campaign had 1–11 clicks. SOP 32 G2 needs 15 clicks for a bid read, and P4.4 says bids hold inside the window. The Day-2 moves below therefore use budget and modifier only. Bid moves are proposed only on the autos, under the P8 pacing exception: spend ran 2× plan.

9Root causes

  • Spend +99% over plan → modifier: T9 ROS premiums left live about 14 hours; no event cap on the $500 aged-deal auto.
  • Auto CPC 5.9–6.5× normal → modifier, not competition: CPC fell the hour after M8.
  • Cooling push CPC $6.5–9.6 → modifier plus bid priced on full-price margin; some event-auction pressure on head Cooling terms.
  • Low TOS share → budget (pushes out by 03:15–10:44) plus premiums moved to ROS plus TOS zeroed on all "out of focus" exacts.
  • Low CVR on the LTSF autos → traffic quality: aged colours that don't convert, served on ROS/PP.
  • Defensive broad over break-even → modifier: PP +100% doubled the PP bid.
  • Twin variation split → process: the event-night ad swap stopped at Navy on 4 campaigns.
  • Cooling push money at all → plan drift: the approved go/no-go ad plan said "pause Cooling, size-only and queen terms"; the event boards pushed Cooling anyway, and paused the most efficient group on Day 1 (Bamboo|Queen, 14% ACoS) for stock.
Detailed analysis · Campaign review

4. Where the waste was

  1. ROS premiums from T9 on autos and broads: $730 of spend across Full-Grey auto ($337.28), King-White auto ($303.01), the B4 LTSF auto ($38.42) and the queen-size broad ($51.63). CPC was $2.40–$4.73 against a $0.58–$2.09 baseline. The ROS clicks converted (12–21% CVR); the cost per click was the problem.
  2. Uncapped aged-deal LTSF auto: $501 at 36.7% ACoS. The aged colours cost $218 for 3 orders (M55).
  3. New experiments opened inside the window: about $60, 0 orders. These were the Conquest PAT ($47.74) and two new tail exacts (~$12). SOP 32 S-E1 says no new experiments enter the window.
  4. Pushes paying $6.5–$10 per TOS click with 0 orders: about $95. These were Bamboo Sheets Cooling, bamboo cool sheets, Cooling Sheets Bamboo, Bamboo Twin Sheets Set, Twin Sheets Bamboo, Twin Bamboo Sheets, Twin Sheets Set Bamboo and Bamboo Sheets Twin Size.
  5. Defensive broad PP +100%: $187 of PP spend at a $3.17 CPC, while TOS on the same terms cost $1.39 and converted at 22%.

Bamboo 6pc (B6) · PED 21–26% · US

DecisionReduce + Fix
DirectionUnits on plan; profit below plan because of ad overspend

Units landed on plan (390 vs 379), but ads ran 2.5–2.7× the plan ($1,383 board / $1,502 Sellerboard vs $557) and TACoS was 5.5% against a 2.3% cap, so profit after reserve came in $442 under plan ($2,277 vs $2,719). The overspend more than explains the profit gap. The full-day ad plan was used up by 10:59 PT. The biggest single bucket was 40 exact push campaigns ($626, ACoS 38%) paying $8–9 TOS clicks for rank that moved with deal sales, not ads. Day 2 is drifting the same way: ranking budgets were raised again to $732 this morning.

Detailed analysis · Campaign review

Bamboo 6pc (product 30, US) — PBDD Day-1 campaign review

Day 1 = Oct 6 2026 (Amazon PT day). Written Oct 7 around 08:00 PT. Read-only review: nothing was staged or changed.

Break-even used: 14.5% ACoS at the deal price (brief and board be). Board beAcos 15.4% is shown as a sensitivity. At the $63.99 deal price, break-even cost per order is $9.28. Max profitable CPC = $9.28 × CVR, for example $2.32 at the 25% TOS CVR B6 had on Oct 6. The list-price break-even of 41.3% in ppc_product_context is not used.

Spend lenses. Campaign lens: $1,788.16 across 174 campaigns. This counts every campaign that carries any B6 ad, so it includes 8 campaigns shared with B4 ($454.76). ASIN lens: $1,501.58, which matches Sellerboard SP. That is what B6 actually paid. It splits into $1,333.40 from B6-only campaigns plus about $168.18 as B6's share of the shared campaigns. The board's hourly feed shows $1,383.49. Oct 6 orders and sales use 7-day attribution and are still filling in; spend, clicks and impressions are final. The tools have almost no Oct 7 campaign rows yet: $10.02 campaign lens, $5.52 ASIN lens. Day-2 numbers below come from the board (about 07:30 PT).

Raw pulls: d1/raw_camp30/. Row-level data plus the full verdict chain for every campaign: d1/camp_30.json.

1. Headline

  • Units were on plan. Ads ran at 2.5–2.7× plan, and that gap explains all of the profit shortfall. Units: 390 vs 378.76 (+3%). Ad spend: $1,383 (board) / $1,502 (ASIN) vs $557 (+$826 / +$944). TACoS: 5.45% (board) / 5.75% (Sellerboard) vs the 2.3% cap. Profit after reserve: $2,276.54 vs $2,718.55 plan (−$442). The overspend is about twice the profit gap.
  • The full-day plan spend was used up by 10:59 PT. Cumulative SP spend reached $574 by 10:59 PT; by then the plan-to-hour spend was $194. By 05:00 PT, $223 (40% of the day's plan) had already gone.
  • What drove the overspend (B6-attributed $1,501.58):
  • 40 exact ranking/push campaigns: $625.93 for 24 orders, ACoS 38.1%. 25 of them spent $270.01 with 0 orders. 18 had CPC ≥ $6 and spent $350.78 for 6 orders (ACoS 84.7%).
  • New LTSF clearance campaigns that were not in the 2.3% plan: $322.82 (Aged Deal auto $252.66, PD-LTSF broad $70.16).
  • A conquest PAT campaign created on event night: $150.11.
  • B6 discovery autos running ROS premiums: $131.18, of which the QUEEN-WHITE auto was $93.08 at 146% ACoS.
  • B6's share of B4-named shared campaigns: about $168.
  • Placement flipped from TOS to ROS. ROS rose to 48% of spend ($857) from 10–13% at baseline (about $78/day). ROS converted at 8.9% against 25.2% at TOS. The cause was the T9 "PLACEMENT PROFIT" ROS modifiers (+148% to +692%) set on event night, which stayed live until 10:39–11:21 PT Oct 6.
  • Paying $8 per TOS click on push terms did not move rank. Against rank_noise.json, every King push term except "king bed bamboo sheets" (17, against a pre-event best of 18) is still inside its pre-event range. "bamboo sheets with corner straps" (4 on Oct 6, 6 on Oct 7, against a pre-event best of 9) is the only clear rank gain, and it bought TOS at a sane $5.49.
  • Variation (Erik #2). The hero BAMBOO-KING-WHITE took 51% of B6 ad spend ($770.95) for 50 units at −$138.71 net. QUEEN-OLIVE took $244.49 for 7 units (net −$185.95). KING-LIGHT PINK took $75.08 for 3 units (net −$85.64), through a B4 auto. The 28-day best seller KING-TAUPE sold 49 units on $0.52 of ads; it was correctly rotated off for low stock (12 days of cover).
  • Day 2 is heading the same way. Units are on plan (45 vs 44.66). Spend is $72.78 vs $65.73. Ranking budgets have been raised again, from $346 at 00:00 PT Oct 6 to $732 as of Oct 7 morning (M47 at 03:51 PT). The pending Oct 8 legs would raise them further (for example $179.29 on "bamboo sheets king" and $75.37 on "bamboo bed").

2.3 Erik's expectations
# Expectation Day-1 evidence Met?
1 Consolidate on the main syntax campaigns; pause everything else; check hourly against the caps 69 B6 campaigns spent ≥ $3. Only 42.3% of B6 search-term spend was on terms owned by a main syntax (Bamboo family 38.8%, Cooling 3.5%); 57.7% ($921.51) was on ASIN, auto or generic terms. The "bamboo sheets" head term (search volume 116k, target rank 9) got $35.91 while 18 tail exacts with CPC ≥ $6 got $350.78. The cap was passed at 10:59 PT and spending continued. No
2 Spend on the preferred, highest-click-rate variation Hero KING-WHITE carries 40 campaigns and 51% of spend, but loses money (−$138.71). QUEEN-OLIVE ($244.49 for 7 units) and KING-LIGHT PINK ($75.08 for 3 units) leaked through autos and the Viscose exact ad group. KING-TAUPE was rotated off for stock, which is a valid exception. Partly
3 Judge by profit including deal fees Profit −$442 vs plan; 30 of the 42 Sellerboard-profiled campaigns lost money before deal fees (−$550 combined). No
4 Ranking terms at the top of search TOS was 100% of spend on most push exacts, but at $7–9 CPC with TOS impression share of 1–31%, and no rank move beyond pre-event noise (except corner straps and king bed). Product TOS share fell to 36% from 56–58% at baseline. Partly (placement right, price wrong, product-level TOS share down)
5 Hourly monitoring, someone accountable The intraday desk (M1–M44) acted from 06:05 PT. The ROS premium stayed live about 13.5 h (21:09 PT Oct 5 → 10:39 PT Oct 6). Capped campaigns climbed from 1 to 31. Several raises were made after the cap was already blown. Partly

2Hour by hour

B6 spent 40% of its full-day ad plan by 05:00 PT and passed the whole-day plan at 10:59 PT ($574 vs $194 planned to that hour). The overnight hours were driven by the auto ROS premiums and the King pushes, which all ran out of budget between 05:09 and 05:32 and were restored at 06:05. After the ROS premiums came off (10:39–11:21) CPC dropped, but the push budgets were raised again at 14:33 and the conquest PAT was funded twice, so spend kept running ahead of plan into the evening. Real intraday rank reads exist for the King terms (about every 6 hours): they drift up smoothly with no step at the 06:05 refund or the 12:24 taper.

3Ranking campaigns

Spending without an incremental rank effect. 39 ranking campaigns spent $626 (42% of B6 spend) at 38% ACoS against a 14.5% break-even; $388 sat above break-even and 24 campaigns took no order. Every King term with any ads rose 3–8 places together, including "bamboo sheets", whose exact was zeroed for the event; the one King push term with no ads at all stayed flat. "Bamboo sheets king" took $69 for 0 orders and gained no more than its cheaper siblings. Only "king bed bamboo sheets" (17, beyond its pre-event best of 18) and "bamboo sheets with corner straps" (4–6 vs a pre-event best of 9, bought at a sane $5.49) moved beyond noise. Structure: about 20 King exacts on separate budgets with duplicates; the 21.5K-volume "bamboo sheets king size" was starved at $5–10 while low-volume exacts got the money; seven King exacts still sit above the 300% ceiling (+420% to +860%).

Detailed analysis · Campaign review
5.1 Exact / ranking (40 campaigns, $625.93, 24 orders, ACoS 38.1%, CPC $4.97)
  • Role: ranking push on King, Queen and Cooling syntaxes. Bid appropriateness: mostly too high. The T11 event layer cut base bids ×0.573 but raised TOS modifiers to hold the TOS price (for example "bamboo sheets king" +407 → +534, "king bed bamboo sheets" +493 → +641, "bamboo king size sheets set" +553). That left effective TOS ceilings at $9–12 until M18 at 12:24 PT. "bamboo king size sheets" runs Fixed bidding at $2.72 × 3.41 = $9.28.
  • CPC: TOS CPCs of $6–9.10 against a break-even TOS CPC of about $2.32. Under SOP-28 F1, a CPC above 1.5× max profitable CPC is unjustifiable outside a sized push, and no push worksheet or allowance was recorded (SOP-32 P5.1, F8).
  • CVR: TOS CVR averaged about 25%, so traffic quality is fine. The problem is price, not relevance.
  • Working:
  • "bamboo sheets with corner straps": rank 9 → 4/6, a real gain; ACoS 20.8%; TOS impression share 25%.
  • "king bamboo sheets": ACoS 14.6%, budget-capped.
  • "bamboo sheets deep pockets king size": ACoS 9%.
  • "sheet set bamboo": ACoS 9.4%.
  • Not working:
  • "bamboo sheets king": $69, 0 orders.
  • "bamboo king size sheets set": $39, 0 orders.
  • Tails "king sheet set bamboo", "bamboo king bedding sets", "top rated", "deep pocket king sheet set", "bamboo bed", "bamboo fitted", spandex, rayon, organic, "Cali King", "Cooling Bedsheets": 1–3 clicks each at $5–8, 0 orders.

The one King push term with no ads at all stayed flat.

Oct 7 test (coordinator item 2): can it be read?

No. At 03:51 PT on Oct 7 all 16 push exacts got a 1.5× budget. Arm A cut TOS on "bamboo sheets king" (+300 → +184%), "king bed bamboo sheets" (+300 → +219%) and B4 "bamboo twin sheets set" (+300 → +165%); the other push exacts kept their boost. - The arms are 3 against 5, unmatched by product, search volume and starting rank. - "bamboo twin sheets set" is tracked by neither ppc_ranks nor the DD radar, so there is no rank to read for it. - Daily noise bands are 7–20 positions wide, far larger than any one-day modifier effect. - Both products are on a PED, so deal velocity moves every rank. - Oct 8 is the settle day: SOP-32 S-E5 and G10 exclude in-window rank reads and the 14 days after.

How to make it readable: compare the arms on same-day placement metrics (TOS click share, TOS CPC, sponsored rank, TOS CVR), hourly, using matched pairs inside one product, for example "bamboo sheets king" against "bamboo king size sheets". Collect at least about 30 TOS clicks per arm before calling it.

Structure issues
  1. About 20 King exact campaigns run on separate budgets, including duplicate pairs (King Size Bamboo Sheets Set / "-2"; King Bed Bamboo Sheets / King Bed Sheets Bamboo). Seven King exacts are still above 300% TOS: +860%, +825%, +515%, +515%, +436%, +436% and +420%.
  2. The highest-volume King term ("bamboo sheets king size", SV 21.5k) was budget-truncated at $5–10, while $69 went to "bamboo sheets king" for 0 orders (SOP-23 G3 and the M5 ordering).
  3. The variation may not match the push. The viscose push advertises QUEEN-WHITE although the product's push is King; check it against the owner's hero rule (Erik #2).
  4. The same $5 overnight cap applied, with run-outs at 00:23 (luxury), 05:09, 05:29 and 05:32. The effective TOS bids of $5.84–9.26 against a deal-price maximum profitable CPC of about $1.78 have no M2 worksheet behind them (SOP-23 F1).
  5. Sibling conflict with B4 on "bamboo sheets" and King terms (SOP-23 G11/F8).

4Auto / Broad / Phrase (and Exact, PAT)

Auto ($131 B6-only plus a $168 share of B4 autos): the Queen White auto paid $4.65 a click (normal $1.04) for 1 order (ACoS 146%), all on ROS. Broad: the B6 discovery broads barely ran; the branded "decolure" broad converted at ACoS 5% on $13 and should be scaled; the PD-LTSF broad took $70 at 36% ACoS. Phrase: negligible. PAT ($235, ACoS 17%): the conquest PAT created on event night took $150 but converted (10 orders, ACoS 22%) — mostly on one competitor ASIN; own-ASIN and defensive PATs ran at 2–14%.

  • Role: discovery. The QW and KING-TAUPE autos got TOS +220/+297 (reverted within 6 minutes) and ROS +307/+148 (live until 10:39 and 11:21 PT).
  • CPC: QW auto $4.65 vs $1.04 baseline; substitutes $4.88. KING-TAUPE auto $1.53.
  • CVR: QW 5% (baseline 3.25%). KING-TAUPE 15% at ACoS 14.9%.
  • Bids: auto base bids of $0.60–1.50 are fine. The premium was the problem (SOP-15; SOP-32 P4.1: no premium without placement evidence).
  • Pending Oct 8 TOS legs (+220, +297, +168) should be cancelled.
5.3 Broad (B6 discovery broads: $1.10; branded "decolure" broad: $13.09; PD-LTSF broad: $70.16)
  • Role: discovery broads were consolidated away, as Erik planned. The branded "decolure" broad was throttled: T9 cut its bid $2.51 → $1.44 and zeroed TOS, so it spent 0.3× baseline while running ACoS 5% and TOS CVR 50%. It should be scaled.
  • PD-LTSF broad: CPC $1.40 (capped at $1.50 by M5), CVR 6%, ACoS 36.2%. Generic king/queen/twin "sheet set" terms on aged SKUs. Pause.
5.4 Phrase
  • No B6 phrase spend on Oct 6 (baseline $0.19/day). "DBS6-SP-LTSF-TWIN-Phrase" and "-FULL-Phrase" are named DBS6 but advertise B4 aged SKUs (paused by M55 at 04:26 PT Oct 7). They carry no B6-attributed spend.
5.5 PAT / conquest (10 campaigns, $234.94, 18 orders, ACoS 17.2%)
  • Conquest (new, created at 20:46 PT Oct 5): $150.11, ACoS 22.3%, 76% ROS. Keep only Love's cabin B0DN1DVKH5.
  • Conversion PATs:
  • B08KQHRDDG -2/-3: ACoS 2.2% and 4.9%. Scale the -2 budget to $10.
  • B08KQHRDDG (first copy): 4 clicks, 0 orders. Duplicate; pause.
  • B0CQ33H4QW: ACoS 14.3%. Keep.
  • B01M16WBW1 (two campaigns): 21 clicks, 1 order. Pause the target under the board L4 rule (15+ clicks with no order).
  • B0B8JLLT45 and B09PYB9C45-2: 0 orders on 2–3 clicks. Hold.
  • Bids: $1.27–2.16; appropriate where the target converts.
5.6 LTSF and defend
  • Aged Deal auto: ACoS 17.8%, near break-even. Cut the budget, keep the campaign.
  • Defensive PAT "Decolure_SP_Exact_PAT_Defensive": ACoS 10.5%, PP 84%. Keep.
  • B4 LTSF autos (Bamboo 4Pcs LTSF, B4 Queen Olive): 0 orders, B4-owned. Flagged to the B4 reviewer.

ROS rose to 48% of spend ($857, against about $78 on a normal day) and converted at 8.9%; TOS converted at 25.2%. Where TOS should get more, within break-even: the branded "decolure" broad (TOS 0 → +44%, bid $2.00; TOS CVR 50%), "king bamboo sheets" (+25 points; ACoS at break-even), the conquest PAT on its converting ASIN (TOS +50% / ROS 0; TOS CVR 28% vs 9%). Where ROS/PP must come off: the Queen White auto (100% ROS), the B01M16WBW1 PATs (100% ROS, 1 order on 21 clicks), and the Viscose exact's product-page spend (40% of it).

Is inventory limiting the push? No for the heroes: King White 6pc 1,248 FBA (187 d normal) and Queen White 6pc 248 FBA + 1,002 inbound (ETA Oct 30). Yes for four colours already rotated off: King Taupe, King Navy, King Purple, Queen Navy.

Verdict. Plan: PED both days; Day-1 plan 379 units → Target: hero White/Black per size with window+14 d cover → Day 1: 390 units (103%); King White 50, King Taupe 49, Queen White 30, King Black 16, Queen Navy 17 → Gap: King Taupe (187 FBA) sells 7.2/d normally and 45-49/d on deal; ~21 d after the event vs a 60-unit shipment Oct 31. Queen Navy 18 FBA, no inbound. → Root cause: deal demand concentrated on colours with thin stock → Direction correct? Yes - Oct 6 ~15:05 rotation paused Queen Navy, King Purple, King Navy, King Taupe in ad groups where King White 6pc serves → Action: Keep all four off ads. Queen White 6pc: keep but no scale-up for the rest of Day 2 (6.9 d at Day-2 pace = SOP-23 YELLOW freeze; 48 d after the event, so no swap). Use King Light Grey 6pc, not King Black 6pc, as the declared King backup. → Expected: King demand lands on King White (1,248 FBA absorbs ~18.6/d including the rotated colours for ~67 d); no stockout in the settle window on advertised SKUs.

8Allocation vs actual

The plan was a 2.3% TACoS cap with money on King/Queen/Cooling pushes and the consolidated main syntaxes. Actual: exact pushes $626, new LTSF clearance campaigns not in the plan $323, a conquest PAT created on event night $150, autos with ROS premiums $131, and B6's share of B4 autos about $168. Decision: the caps below add up to about $555, on the $557 plan; anything above plan-to-hour by more than 20% at 12:00 or 16:00 cuts the aged-deal auto first.

9Root causes

  • Profit below plan → spend, not demand: units were on plan; the $826–944 overspend is about twice the profit gap.
  • $8–9 TOS clicks on pushes → modifier (+534–641%) on bids priced for full-price margin; no worksheet behind the ceilings.
  • Push budgets out by 05:32 → the event layer's $5 overnight cap, then refunded and re-raised all day.
  • ROS at 48% of spend → T9 ROS premiums live until late morning.
  • Rank not incremental → rank follows deal velocity on the discounted King SKU; ad spend added nothing measurable on top.
  • Losses on Queen Olive and King Light Pink → variation: stock rotation and a B6 SKU inside a B4 auto.
  • Cooling money on B6 at all → plan drift: the go/no-go ad plan said "pause Cooling and size-only" for B6; the board objective added Cooling back.

Even at its baseline of $431/day, the exact ranking programme alone would have used 77% of the $557 cap, so the cap was structurally incompatible with running the push programme unchanged. On top of that, Day 1 added items the cap never covered: $323 of LTSF clearance, $150 of new conquest, a $119 ROS premium on autos, and $168 of B6's share of the B4 autos and defensive PATs.

What the money bought: - Exact pushes: $549 at TOS, $5–9 CPC, 24 orders, mostly KING-WHITE. - Aged Deal auto: 190 clicks at $1.33, 22 orders, ACoS 17.8%, Sellerboard profit +$161 before deal fee. - Conquest: Love's cabin B0DN1DVKH5 gave 8 orders at 16.1%; the rest gave 2 orders for $64. - Autos: ROS substitutes clicks at $4.65–4.88.

Limits and what could not be verified for this product

12. What could not be verified

  • Campaign-level hourly spend. No tool provides it. The timing above is rebuilt from run-out times, move times and the product hourly series.
  • Per-campaign B6 slice of the 8 B4-shared campaigns. Only the total is derivable (about $168.18). KING-LIGHT PINK ($75.08) is the confirmed B6 SKU in DBS4 FULL-GREY.
  • Live modifier and budget values. The decision record is not a verified read of live state: many Oct 6–7 moves are unverified or conflict (see modifier_audit.md). Several board run-out budgets conflict with the record. For example, luxury shows $30 at 00:23 PT on the board vs $5 per T11; "bamboo sheets king" shows $60 on the board vs $50 per the 06:05 move. Board values are quoted as board data.
  • Keyword × advertised-ASIN click rates. Variation per keyword could not be measured; Erik #2 was judged at ASIN level.
  • Oct 7 campaign rows. Effectively empty in the tools (report lag); Day-2 so-far comes from the board only.
  • Sellerboard figures. Campaign profit and TOS impression share are UTC-day and whole-campaign, and profit excludes the PED deal fee. Sellerboard's Conquest spend ($137.15) differs from ecotero ($150.11).
  • Keyword lens total. It sums to $1,596.22 vs the $1,501.58 product total (tool inconsistency).
  • Sellerboard ppc_bidding_history. Not used; the decision record already covers the timing.

Does Day 1 meet Erik's expectations?
  1. Consolidated on main syntax campaigns, everything else paused: No. - About 200 Satin campaign rows spent on Oct 6, including 42 exact ranking campaigns. - Event night (Oct 5 20:44–21:59 PT) added 39 new Satin 4pc campaigns (create_campaign 22 + 17) and about 1,450 moves in all (T9 512, T11 241, TAPER 133, untagged 570). SOP 32 S-E1 says no new experiments enter a window. - LTSF/clearance went from 5.7% of baseline spend to 22.3%.
  2. Spend on the preferred, highest-CTR variation: No, on the queen terms (section 1.D). White Queen V2 took 98% of exact spend on "satin sheets queen" and "satin sheets queen size", at CTR 0.43–0.44% against Queen Black's 2.66%.
  3. Judge by profit with deal fees included: not met at campaign level. Only "Queen Satin Sheet Set" broad (9.2%) and own-ASIN PAT (10.5%) are at or under 10.6%.
  4. Ranking terms at TOS: mostly yes. - Black "satin sheets" exact was 97% TOS. On the crawler, "satin sheets" ranked 5 on Oct 6 and 2 on Oct 7; the Oct 7 reading is better than any pre-event day (pre-event range 3–5). - White V2 was only 68% TOS, with 30% of its spend on product pages. - "Satin sheets queen" rank went 3 (Oct 6) → 9 (Oct 7), worse than any pre-event day (5–6). - "Silk sheets queen" rank went 9 → 10, also worse than the pre-event range (6–8).
  5. Hourly monitoring: yes. Moves desk M5–M65 ran through the day. But several raises (M26, M33, M38, M65) were made without a named allowance (SOP 32 P8.2).

3Ranking campaigns

Defend met, at a loss. 42 ranking campaigns spent $571 (63% of Satin spend) at 41% ACoS; $424 sat above break-even. At the deal price the margin is $2.54 a unit, so the SOP caps the profitable CPC at about $0.85; Day-1 CPCs were $2.02–3.93. "satin sheets" #2 on Oct 7 is better than any pre-event day on DataRova (Data Dive reads 9), and ads aren't needed to explain it. "satin sheets queen" (#9 DR / #3 DD) is inconclusive. "silk sheets queen" slipped to #10 while TOS-funded. Half of the White V2 budget went to "satin sheets queen size", already ranked #2.

Detailed analysis · Ranking review

S4 – Satin 4pc (37) · objective "Defend page 1" · BE 10.6% at deal price (thin margin)

Verdict: the defend objective is met, but at a loss. Page 1 held. At the deal price the margin is $2.54 per unit, which is thin (under $6). SOP-23 P2 step 7 therefore caps expected CPC at $0.85; Day-1 CPCs on these campaigns ran $2.02–3.93. - Spend: 42 ranking campaigns spent $570.58, which is 62.5% of the $912.83 attributed product spend. - Efficiency: ACoS was 41.2%, so $423.72 was above break-even. - Rank result: page 1 held on the head terms. "silk sheets queen" slipped despite TOS funding.

Structure issues
  1. Two exact targets share one $180 ranking budget in the satin-queen campaign (SOP-23 P6 calls for single-keyword structure). Half the money went to a term already held at #2.
  2. Bids are set for full-price economics. At the deal price this product is thin class (SOP-23 P2 step 7).
  3. The satin-queen exact advertises WHITE-QUEEN while the "satin sheets" exact uses QUEEN-BLACK. Check this against the hero rule.
Detailed analysis · Search-term and negation review

The hero test (M56, 30 days) agrees: Black CVR 13.5% vs 9.4% for other colours, p 0.025. White got the queen-term spend; Black converts.

Day-1 SKU sell-through (board): SATIN-QUEEN-BLACK sold 61 of 105 committed, SATIN-FULL-BLACK 18 of 61, SATIN-QUEEN-GREY 16 of 23. White Queen is not in the top 10 sellers.

What the $0.94 means. At the deal price Queen Black earns about $0.94 per unit before ads (thread figure). My own arithmetic gives $4.26 before deal fees: $23.96 − 15% referral − FBA $6.82 − landed cost $9.29. At Black's 32% CVR, break-even CPC is therefore $0.30–$1.36, against the $2.14 Black actually paid.

With the PED live, no Satin exact or ranking campaign can pay for itself on Day 2. Only these can be justified: - (a) branded and own-ASIN defence at floor; - (b) LTSF lanes, judged on cost per aged unit against $17.07; - (c) one declared-loss push: Black "satin sheets" at $70 as the SOP 23 loss ceiling.

Everything else should be trimmed.

7Stock and inventory

Not limiting for the event; a Q4 flag. 15,139 FBA + 1,229 inbound; 52 / 87 / 138 days of cover. Queen Black (hero) has 1,604 units, 83 days at normal pace and no inbound, so it runs out around Dec 29 — reorder now for BFCM. King Black has 2,450 units, which supports swapping the generic King campaigns from King Grey to Black. Red Queen has 3 units: move its colour campaigns to King Red (233 + 402 inbound) and pause "Red Silk Sheets Queen". Aged Queen Grey 1,088 units belongs in the LTSF lane, not the discovery broads.

9Root causes

  • Units short → deal execution: the LD price wasn't live until ~07:40 and the deal records conflict (cancelled / confirmed / "has issues"); then the weaker response to a discount than bamboo (~1.4× vs ~3×).
  • Ad loss → economics: at $23.96 the margin is $2.54/unit ($0.94 for Queen Black), so a $2 click needs a near-certain conversion.
  • Low CTR on the queen terms → wrong variation: White Queen at 0.43% vs Black at 2.66%.
  • LTSF overspend → budget raised without a cost-per-unit stop rule.
  • Spend sprawl → 39 campaigns added inside the event window.

SS-Satin 4Pcs - LTSF Campaigns (345821251270943)
  • Plan: LTSF auto lane. T9 (Oct 5 20:43 PT) set TOS +825% / ROS +793% from 0; M8 10:39 PT ROS -> 0; M15 11:20 PT TOS -> +300%. Budget $70, ran out 09:02 PT Day 1. Not touched by Day-2 containment ('clearance kept as is', M60).
  • Target: LTSF accepted CPA for SS Satin (not stated in the record; Satin 4pc reference $13.52-$17.07); BE ACoS 27.9%.
  • Day-1 result: $71.40, 30 clk, CPC $2.38 vs baseline $0.36 (6.6x), 2 orders = $35.70 per unit, ACoS 108.3%. TOS $47.64 (22 clk, CVR 9.1%), ROS $23.76 (8 clk, 0 orders).
  • Gap: Cost per unit ~2x any accepted LTSF CPA; ACoS 80 pts over BE.
  • Root cause: The T9 +825% TOS premium (still +300%) turned a $0.36-CPC clearance auto into a $2.38-CPC TOS buyer; SOP 32 P4.1 forbids premiums without placement evidence and P4.3 the window ceiling is lower, not higher.
  • Is the current direction correct? Wrong; and excluded from containment.
  • Required action (Day 2): TOS +300% -> 0 now; budget $70 -> $25. No bid change (P4.4). Revert nothing on Oct 8 (T9 premium has no evidence).
  • Expected outcome: CPC back toward $0.4-0.6; ~$25/day; cost per aged unit under $17.

Planning thread audit: plan, dates and what happened

The whole planning thread (Sep 23 → Oct 7, 97 messages) was read with every message time converted to UTC, PT, ET and PKT, together with the operating brief, the projection workbook, the go/no-go and committed-units files and the final-plan artifact. The detail is below; the conclusions:

  • The critical path was late almost everywhere. Erik's plan went out Sat Oct 3 21:09 ET, 1 h 51 m before its first step. Of 15 steps: 1 on time (US go/no-go, 2 h early), 7 late (test upload +10 h, PED prices +6 h, LD details +25 h, allocation +4 h, final upload +10 h, error check +1 h, PPC armed +9 h), and 5 with no evidence of being done: the war-room roster, the Featured Offer check, the "+50% event bid rule" check, the TikTok/DTC price check and the final check. Canada had no test upload and no units until Oct 5.
  • Decisions left to default. Umair's request to cancel 13 deals was never approved, so five ran unplanned with no stock or margin check (US Satin Fitted LD, Cooling Pillowcases LD, Closet Organizer BD; CA Satin Fitted BD, CA Sleephoria Satin BD). Nobody decided the Satin PED, so it switched on by default at 19:40 PT Oct 6, although the board recommended pulling it (Queen Black at the PED price makes −$0.06 a unit after ads). The four priority variations not raised in allocation got no impact estimate or mitigation, which Erik asked for.
  • Rules until Oct 8: Broken hourly ad caps (B4 and B6 over cap in all 24 hours; B4, B6 and S4 each spent more on Day 1 than their whole 2-day budget), the +50% bid rule (T9 set TOS up to +900%), and consolidation on main syntaxes (552 campaigns spent). Kept no PED on a parent with its top variation out of stock. Unknown prices on other channels; three primary-image changes on B4/B6 listings during the event (who made them is not established).
  • The executed PPC plan contradicted the approved one. The go/no-go ad plan for B4 and B6 said "pause Cooling, size-only and queen terms" and keep spend on the Bamboo syntaxes; the event boards then pushed Cooling on both products.
  • Erik's questions: six were never answered — the Satin post-LD plan, the strategy per product coming out of Prime Day, deal fees in the profitability analysis, maximising SKUs per PED, the parents left out of the plan, and the cancellation approval. The answer to "why does spend keep drifting from targets" did not hold: it drifted again on Day 1.
  • Still open for BFCM: the regular deals on the calendar Oct 12–Nov 2 for B4/B6/S4/S6 (the real lookback risk), the written Seller Support confirmation that PBDD prices are excluded (asked Sep 25, never received), who runs the Oct 8 reverts and when, and the BFCM plan due Oct 10.
Full planning audit (timeline, per-product plan, rules, questions, framework gaps)

PBDD planning thread audit: plan vs execution (US + Canada)

Generated 2026-10-07 15:05 UTC. Thread C05SVU9BDEF / 1790171225.256739: 97 messages (parent + 96 replies), Wed Sep 23 13:47 UTC to Wed Oct 07 12:53 UTC. Times: ET = America/New_York (EDT), PT = PDT, PKT = UTC+5. Every number below comes from the thread, its attachments, the linked artifacts (outside-org boards, treated as data), the live-board extracts already in the scratchpad, ppc_decisions (all_dec.json), d1/board_us_plan.json, d1/hourly_products.json, modifier_audit.md, or Data Dive listing changes. Raw pulls: d1/raw_plan/.

Headline

  1. The plan was posted late and almost every pre-event step slipped. Erik's critical path went out Sat Oct 3 21:09 ET, 1 h 51 m before its first deadline. Of 15 critical-path steps, 1 was on time (US go/no-go, approved 09:55 ET Sun, 2 h early), 7 were late (test upload +10h26m, PED prices +6h26m, LD details +25h, allocation +3h39m, final upload +9h57m, error check +57m, PPC armed +9h28m), 5 have no evidence of being done (war-room roster, Featured Offer check, +50% event bid rule check, TikTok/DTC price check, final check), break-even ad spend was covered early by the go/no-go board rather than its owner, and the kickoff was probably held but its outcome was not posted. The Canada test upload and Canada units were also missing on Oct 5. The brief's internal Oct 1 PED target was missed by ~2.5 days and the Sep 25 written lookback confirmation never arrived.
  2. During the event, three decisions were left to default. (a) 13 deal cancellations requested by Umair at Oct 5 06:32 ET were never approved in writing; 5 ran anyway (US Satin Fitted LD, US Sleephoria Cooling Pillowcases LD, US Closet BD, CA Satin Fitted BD, CA Sleephoria Satin 4pc BD) with no stock or committed-unit check. (b) The S4 Day-2 PED switched on at 19:40 PT because nobody answered M37 (the board recommended removing it: Queen Black $0.94 margin before ads, -$0.06 after). (c) The 4 priority variations not raised (B4 Queen White, B6 King/Queen Taupe, S4 Queen Black) got no impact estimate or mitigation.
  3. The PPC rules were broken on Day 1. Ads were supposed to sit only on main syntaxes with everything else paused and every product inside its cap hour by hour. In fact 552 campaigns spent; account ad spend was $7,682 vs $3,595 planned (x2.1); B4, B6 and S4 each spent more on Day 1 than their whole 2-day event budget; B4 and B6 were over cap in all 24 hours, S4 from 07:00 PT and it finished at 10.84%, above its 10.6% break-even. The '+50% event bid rule' was never checked; instead the T9 run ('one move, no cap') set TOS up to +900%.
  4. Results beat plan on volume and profit thanks to the discount, organic sales and Canada, not PPC (Day 1 review: 1,718 units vs 1,421, profit after reserve $9,422 vs $5,031). S4 underdelivered (294 vs 356 units; LD added ~1.4x; defend terms lost 4-6 places). B6 profit was below plan ($2,277 vs $3,100) because of ad overspend.
  5. Erik's questions: 31 tracked. 6 were never answered or resolved in the thread (S4 post-LD plan, post-PD strategy per product, deal fees in profitability, SKUs per PED, Umair's uncovered-parents question, the cancellation approval), 9 were only partly answered, and the PPC drift answer ([29]) did not hold. The committed-units edit trick carries an account risk Erik himself flagged (Amazon may flag the account and revoke deal privileges).

Committed-units edit trick, account-risk caveat. Erik [70] offered a workaround for editing committed units on a running deal and said himself that it "should not be used extensively, as Amazon may flag our account and possibly revoke the deal privileges". It was not used on the running S4 LD (Joseph [73]: "Amazon locks LD quantities while it runs"). The Silk LD was raised before it started by hand on the deal edit page (ledger 19:46 CT). Amazon's own template note says committed units are not hard limits and a SKU starts deactivating at 90% of its commitment. Any future use needs a named approver, a log line and a limit per event.

5. Framework gaps for BFCM

Area Gap the thread exposes What to fix before BFCM
Price floor, price ceiling and the SGR/STR process Erik's parent post asks for a price floor and BFCM price ceiling and how SGR is implemented; nothing in the thread sets either. The brief's floor ((COGS+FBA)/0.625) was overridden for B6 (fails at $64.35 vs $71.98) and S4 PED (LTSF override) without a named approver or stated cost in the thread. STR coverage fell from 72.6% (Aug 3) to 12.9% (Sep 21); restoration (Oct 8-20) is not scheduled in the thread. Per-SKU floor and BFCM max-deal price in the plan file before any submission; overrides named with cost and approver; STR restoration calendar owned by AB.
PED vs LD/BD decision protocol The brief has gates (offer, floor, inventory, PPC break-even, second-day) but the thread never applied them as a protocol; S4 Day-2 PED and Silk PED/LD were left undecided. Measured on Day 1: bamboo PED added ~3.1x, satin LD only ~1.4x; hero-only PED pays for 0 of 12 products. Write the measured lifts into the gate (category response factor); a default for each 'second day' decided before the event; a decision deadline (e.g. LD end - 3 h).
Deal eligibility Six SKUs failed the rating minimum and 33 needed >20% because our own September Best Deals set the 30-day low (B6 $72.24 Sep 26-30; S4 $25 Aug 22-Sep 4). The written Seller Support confirmation that PBDD prices are excluded from the 30/60-day lookback (P0-6, due Sep 25) was never posted. Eligibility pre-check 30 days out (rating, 30/60-day lows, minimum discount); keep a deal-floor register; get the lookback ruling in writing.
Allocation logic Three different rules in 3 days: 1.5x projection with 30-day cover (Oct 4 CSV), 80%/60% trigger with forward >= 10 DOH over 90 days ([54]), then stock-safe template upload. Raises were incremental until Erik objected ([74]). Amazon deactivates at 90% of committed units, so an 80% trigger leaves little room. 4 priority variations were never raised and no impact/mitigation was posted. Canada BD caps (B6 King White 11/11) had no owner. One allocation rule set before the event: commit stock-safe units up front (forward floor stated), reserve per hero, alert at 70%, explicit owner per marketplace.
War-room coverage, roles and permissions No roster or channel posted (due Oct 3 / Sun 14:00 ET). Umair offline during the allocation window; Joseph could not edit live deals until 20:31 UTC; AB promised validation 7 min after start; the moves desk depended on one approver whose last batch was ~19:05 CT; Day-2 PED decision (M37) got no answer. Named primary + backup per desk per shift with Seller Central permissions tested T-1; a default rule for any decision not answered by its deadline.
PPC control Caps were product-level but the loader did not enforce them: T9 'one move, no cap' set TOS to +900%; push budgets were cut to $5 floors; 552 campaigns spent vs 'everything else paused'; Day 1 spend 2.1x plan; the +50% event bid rule was never checked; 4,084 Oct 8 reverts have no owner/time. Hard caps in the loader (product spend and TOS ceiling); pause list applied and verified T-1; push envelope separate from profit cap; revert owner and time fixed in the plan.
Deal calendar hygiene and cancellations Umair asked for approval to cancel 13 deals on Oct 5 10:32 UTC (after the Oct 4 cut-off the board recommended); no approval recorded; 5 ran unplanned with no stock or committed-unit check; MX Best Deals drew US stock unplanned. Cancellation list approved with the go/no-go; one deal register across US/CA/MX.
Decisions still open Regular deals still on the calendar Oct 12-Nov 2 on B4, B6, S4 and S6 (S4 BD Oct 16-28 and LD Nov 2; B4/B6 Oct 15-28) would lower the BFCM ceiling if deeper than 5%; Seller Support written confirmation of the lookback exclusion; who runs the Oct 8 reverts and when; post-PD per-product strategy ([47]); non-hero spend analysis ([95]); BFCM plan (due Oct 10, submissions Oct 16-20). Owner + date for each, tracked in the BFCM plan.

Variation spend: the analysis Erik asked for

Erik asked why only 52–60% of spend went to the hero colour. The analysis covers 100% of Day-1 SP spend by advertised SKU (Sellerboard, matching the ad data to the cent).

Bamboo 4pcBamboo 6pcSatin 4pc
Hero share of SP spend52.2%60.1%51.3%
Hero share without LTSF75.7%76.5%66.5%
LTSF clearance spend$585$323$209
Hero share after the fixes (R1–R8)68.4% (88.5% ex-LTSF)68.6% (84.4%)67.4% (87.4%)
  • Erik is right that LTSF doesn't explain it. Shared multi-colour ad groups account for about $1 — almost every manual campaign carries one ad. The non-hero spend comes from how campaigns are built: LTSF autos taking the head term (88% of "bamboo sheets" spend on B4), one discovery auto running 8+ non-hero colours (Full Grey, $337, no stock reason), Satin King campaigns built on King Grey (King Black has 2,450 units), and an engine switch of four Queen silk campaigns from Black to White on child conversion — the metric Erik rejected.
  • CTR supports Erik's rule. On the same search term the hero had the higher CTR in 3 of 4 comparisons ("satin sheets" 2.66% vs 0.85%; "bamboo sheets twin" 6.67% vs 1.07%; B6 "bamboo sheets" 2.33% vs 0.87%). Directional only: placements differ and impressions by advertised child aren't available.
  • Legitimate exceptions (all under 14 days of cover at deal pace): B4 Queen White → Light Blue (1.9 days), B6 Queen White → Olive (8.3 days), B4 Twin White → Navy (5.3 days), B4 Full White (out of stock) → Olive. Pausing the remaining Queen White 4pc ads until its 732 inbound lands lowers hero share on purpose.
  • One correction to the swap list: walling "bamboo sheets" out of the LTSF autos (R1) is held until after the event — the term converts there and the hero exact is held at $0.83 for the event, so the wall would cut live orders. Use bid and budget cuts on those autos instead (in the B4 and B6 decision tables).
Full variation analysis

Day-1 (Oct 6) US ad spend by advertised variation: Bamboo 4pc (59), Bamboo 6pc (30), Satin 4pc (37)

Read-only analysis. Nothing was staged or changed. Machine-readable version: d1/variation.json. Cell-level detail (campaign × advertised SKU × bucket): d1/raw_variation/cells_bucketed.json.

Answer to Erik

  • The 52–60% figure is correct. Hero colour share of Day-1 SP spend was 52.2% for B4, 60.1% for B6 and 51.3% for S4.
  • LTSF explains about half of the gap, not all of it. Without the LTSF campaigns the hero share is 75.7% / 76.5% / 66.5%.

  • The rest is structural. Very little of it is Amazon choosing between colours inside shared ad groups. The shared-ad-group bucket (e) holds $1.09 in total, because almost every manual campaign carries one ad. The non-hero dollars come from five places: 1. The LTSF aged-SKU autos captured the head term. On "bamboo sheets", the DBS4 aged auto spent $122.72 of $139.26 (88%) and the DBS6 aged auto spent $34.99 of $35.91. The hero exact campaign "Bamboo Sheets (VHSV) Exact" served $0 of that term. This spend sits inside the LTSF bucket, but it is ranking-term leakage, not clearance. 2. A multi-SKU discovery auto, DBS4-SP-Auto…DO-BAMBOO-FULL-GREY ($337, ACOS 52.8%), advertised 8+ non-hero colours across 4pc and 6pc. Bucket (g): $158 on B4 and $81 on B6. 3. On satin, the campaign structure itself picks King Grey for every generic King keyword, even though King Black has 2,450 FBA units: $104. On Oct 6 the engine also swapped four Queen silk campaigns from Queen Black to Queen White, based on child-level CVR, which contradicts Erik's CTR-plus-parent rule: $28.7. 4. Stock rotations, which are legitimate exceptions:

    Size (product) Hero child and cover at deal pace Child serving instead Day-1 $
    Queen (B4) Queen White: 51 FBA, 1.9 d Light Blue $49
    Queen (B6) Queen White 6pc: 8.3 d Olive $152
    Twin (B4) Twin White 4pc: 5.3 d Navy $41
    Full (B4) Full White out of stock Olive $14
  1. Colour-named keywords and own-brand defensive PAT. These are correct as they are: $26–$37 per product. - Fixing items 1–3 would lift hero share to about 68% / 69% / 67% overall, and to about 89% / 84% / 87% excluding LTSF. This assumes the moved dollars are re-spent on the hero ad. Stock-limited and LTSF dollars are not moved.

Why the earlier "shared ad group" claim was wrong

The thread's first claim was that 61–90% of impressions went to non-hero colours in shared ad groups. It was corrected to 29–51% and about $70 across 17 ads. Day-1 data shows that mixed-colour manual campaigns barely exist. Non-hero dollars come from:

  • campaigns whose single ad is a non-hero child (structure, rotation, or engine swap);
  • autos and broads that carry many colours (LTSF and Auto FULL-GREY).

The engine's M56 hero rule (Oct 7, owner-approved) already paused Queen Grey and White Queen inside the satin autos. On Day 1 that was $4.78.

Hero vs non-hero: CTR (primary) and CVR

Limits
  • CTR by advertised variation needs impressions by ad. No available tool reports that, and it was not attributable inside multi-ASIN campaigns.
  • So the comparison below uses only single-ad campaigns (one of our ASINs, observed, with at least 90% of the campaign's dollars on it). Keyword mixes differ between the two groups, so the CTR gap is partly a keyword effect.
  • Conversion here is the campaign's 7-day attributed orders ÷ clicks. That counts any child bought from the brand (halo), which is close to Erik's parent-level view. It cannot be split per click by child.
  • Oct-6 orders are still filling in.

14

Account-level conclusion and Day-2 priorities

Where we stand against the plan

The US beat its Day-1 plan on units (+10%) and profit (board +$1.0–1.5K after reserve on the deal products; more on Sellerboard's costs), but it did so despite the PPC, not because of it. Deal-product ad spend ran 2.3× plan, every deal product ran above its TACoS cap in most hours, and ad ACoS was two to three times break-even. The plan's caps were right: the go/no-go model said uncapped ads would turn a +$10K event into a loss on several products, and the event only stayed profitable because units beat plan and 75–80% of them were organic.

Who is carrying and who is dragging

  • Carrying: Bamboo 4pc (profit +$1.2K vs plan, 1.18× pace on Day 2), with the efficient non-deal products (Sleephoria Cooling 4pc, Cooling Fitted, Satin 6pc) running ahead of a normal day at TACoS under their normal caps.
  • Dragging: Bamboo 6pc (profit −$442 vs plan, all of it ad overspend), Satin 4pc (units −26%, ads at a loss at the deal price, PED left on by default), Sleephoria Satin (−$94) and Satin Fitted (−$20 with an unplanned LD).

Is the ranking strategy working?

No, not as run. On B4 and B6 the ranking campaigns spent about $1,000 (about $550 above break-even) and the only rank moves beyond normal daily noise were "bamboo sheets twin" (one feed), "king bed bamboo sheets" and "corner straps". King terms rose together whether or not they had ads, so rank followed the discounted SKU's sales velocity. Satin held page 1 on "satin sheets" but at a loss, and Silk never started. The mechanics defeated the strategy: push budgets cut to $5 overnight, bids priced on the full-price margin, ceilings above 300%, money spread over about 30 low-volume exacts while the highest-volume terms (B6 "bamboo sheets king size", B4 "bamboo cooling sheets") were starved or paused.

Where the biggest spend gaps are

  1. Placement premiums from the event-night T9 run — rest-of-search boosts of +377% to +692% on autos and broads (about $860 on B4 and B6 alone) left live for about 14 hours.
  2. Exact pushes paying $5–10 a click — about $978 above break-even across B4, B6 and S4.
  3. Uncapped LTSF clearance — $1,086 in the US, outside the event registry and plan.
  4. Campaigns created inside the event window — the conquest PATs, 39 new Satin campaigns, new non-deal broads that are still leaking on Day 2.
  5. Wrong variation — Satin queen terms on White (0.43% CTR), King terms on Grey, B6 SKUs inside B4 autos.

How inventory changes the decisions

  • Inventory is not holding back the push on any product. B4 has 19 days of cover at Day-1 pace (102 at normal), B6 18 (101), Satin 52 (138); the push SKUs have room: B4 King White 1,784 units, B6 King White 1,248, Satin Queen Black 1,604.
  • The thin colours are already off ads — keep them off: B4 Queen White (51 units, inbound flagged overdue; swap back at ≥ 250), B6 King Taupe (runs out ~Oct 29, 60 arriving Oct 31), B6 Queen White 6pc (6.9 days today, 1,002 due Oct 30: hold spend), B4 Twin White (stays on Navy).
  • Campaigns still pointed at out-of-stock SKUs on other products: B4 Full White (8 campaigns), Sleephoria Cooling King Graphite (19), Satin Fitted Queen White autos, Cooling Fitted King Cool Blue (5), Decolure Cooling Queen Graphite Grey. Each has a named in-stock replacement in its product section.
  • Q4 flag: Satin Queen Black has no inbound and runs out around Dec 29 at normal pace — reorder now for BFCM. Aged-stock fees (projected per month): B6 $2,499, Sleephoria Satin $2,322, Satin 4pc $1,487, Satin 6pc $1,145 — these are the post-event clearance priorities.

Day-2 priorities, in order

  1. Before tonight: cancel or rewrite the pending Oct 8 legs (10 on B4, about 10 on B6, 24 account-wide at TOS ≥ 300%). They restore the T9 premiums, not the pre-event values.
  2. Now: cap what caused the overspend — B4 Full Grey auto $40, King White auto $60, aged-deal auto $500 → $200; B6 Queen White auto $10, aged-deal auto $250 → $100, PD-LTSF broad paused; Satin LTSF broad $225 → $150 with a $17.07-per-unit stop.
  3. Now: take every TOS modifier above 300% down to 300% (21 exacts, incl. +860% and +900%), set ROS/PP to 0 on the T9 leftovers, and remove the event-night TOS boosts on the non-deal clearance autos and broads (Sleephoria Satin +165–300%, Satin Fitted +80–85%).
  4. Reprice the pushes to the deal margin and put the money on volume: B6 money onto "bamboo sheets king size" (21.5K searches) at ≤ $4.80; B4 Twin White and Queen exacts funded; Cooling capped with a stop-loss; Satin "satin sheets" as one declared-loss defence at $70.
  5. Fix the variations Erik flagged: Satin queen terms and four silk campaigns back to Queen Black; King campaigns to King Black (one Grey control); non-hero ads out of the B4 Full Grey auto; pause B4 Queen White ads for stock.
  6. Negations: remove 7021 ("cooling sheets queen" on the B6 Queen White auto); upload the taxonomy-irrelevant workbook negatives; hold relevant event-day terms to Oct 13; route "silk pillowcase" from the broad to the exact.
  7. Silk LD (live until 18:05): exact TOS +100%, $40 cap, back to $1.00 / TOS 0 at 18:05.
  8. Read the hourly board at 12:00, 16:00 and 20:00 PT against plan-to-hour spend; any product more than 20% over cuts its LTSF lane first. Read the ranking test on same-day TOS click share, CPC and sponsored rank, not on tomorrow's organic rank.

Decisions that need you or Erik today

  • Ranking investment caps above break-even for the rest of the event: B4 $100, B6 $150, Satin only the "satin sheets" defence, Silk $40.
  • Whether to keep the Satin PED live for the rest of Day 2 (it switched on by default; Queen Black loses about $0.06 a unit after ads at the PED price).
  • SOP-29 P12: negatives in-window now, or all on Oct 8.
  • The regular deals on the calendar Oct 12–Nov 2 for B4/B6/S4/S6 (cancel or keep no deeper than the September lows), and chasing the written lookback confirmation.
